architecture_decisions.recommendation: Changed MariaDB adapter to use binary protocol for regular queries to preserve decimal precision
architecture_decisions.rationale: The MariaDB driver's default `query` method uses text protocol which can lose precision for large decimal values. The `execute` method uses binary protocol that preserves exact numeric precision. This is critical for financial applications where decimal precision matters.
alternatives_considered: Keep using text protocol and accept precision loss
Use a different MySQL driver that always uses binary protocol

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented phantom queries for transaction operations when using binary protocol
architecture_decisions.rationale: The MariaDB binary protocol doesn't support transaction operations (BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT). To maintain transaction compatibility while using binary protocol for queries, we use `query` method (text protocol) for transaction operations only. This hybrid approach gives us precision for data queries while maintaining transaction support.
alternatives_considered: Disable transactions entirely when using binary protocol
Switch back to text protocol for all operations when transactions are needed

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added proper error handling for transaction operations with try-catch-finally blocks
architecture_decisions.rationale: Transaction operations now use explicit error handling with `try-catch-finally` to ensure cleanup happens even if transaction commands fail. This prevents connection leaks and ensures proper resource management.
alternatives_considered: Let errors bubble up without cleanup
Implement retry logic for failed transaction operations

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created comprehensive end-to-end test for decimal precision preservation
architecture_decisions.rationale: Added a dedicated test suite that validates large decimal values maintain precision through create/update operations. The test uses Prisma.Decimal type with extremely large values (30-digit precision) to ensure the binary protocol fix works correctly.
alternatives_considered: Add integration tests to existing test files
Skip testing due to complexity of decimal precision testing

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated existing tests to handle Float32 precision variance
architecture_decisions.rationale: When using binary protocol, FLOAT values are transmitted as 32-bit IEEE 754 floats, which can have different precision than text representation. Updated test assertions to accept either the exact value or the Float32 representation to account for this variance.
alternatives_considered: Force all FLOAT values to be transmitted as DECIMAL
Skip FLOAT tests when using binary protocol

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated tracing tests to include MariaDB adapter in synthetic transaction queries
architecture_decisions.rationale: Since MariaDB adapter now uses phantom queries for transactions (mixing binary protocol for data and text protocol for transactions), it needs to be included in the list of adapters that use synthetic transaction queries for proper tracing behavior.
alternatives_considered: Create separate tracing logic for MariaDB

implementation_summary:
The implementation addresses precision loss issues in MySQL/MariaDB by switching the MariaDB adapter to use the binary protocol for regular queries. This was achieved by changing `client.query()` to `client.execute()` in the `MariaDbQueryable` class, which ensures decimal values maintain exact precision during transmission.

However, since the binary protocol doesn't support transaction operations, a hybrid approach was implemented. Transaction operations (BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT) continue to use the text protocol via `client.query()`, while all data queries use the binary protocol. This required making the connection object accessible in the transaction class and updating all transaction methods to use direct query calls instead of going through the existing `executeRaw` method.

The solution includes comprehensive error handling with try-catch-finally blocks to ensure proper cleanup of connections even when transaction operations fail. The `usePhantomQuery` flag was set to `true` to indicate that transaction operations are handled separately from regular queries.

To validate the fix, a dedicated test suite was created that exercises large decimal values (up to 30 digits) through create and update operations. Existing tests were also updated to handle Float32 precision variance that occurs when using the binary protocol. The tracing tests were updated to include MariaDB in the list of adapters that use synthetic transaction queries, ensuring observability tools work correctly with this hybrid approach. New files introduced by this change: `packages/client/tests/functional/issues/29160-mysql-precision-loss/_matrix.ts`, `packages/client/tests/functional/issues/29160-mysql-precision-loss/prisma/_schema.ts`, `packages/client/tests/functional/issues/29160-mysql-precision-loss/tests.ts`.
